design:
Child epic of the integrated petrochemical and polymer platform (bn op-9941 / see #77 programme).

**Fidelity target: Engineering model**

The refinery -> petrochemical bridge. Feed: hydrotreated naphtha. Products:
reformate, **H2**, light gas.

Reaction families: paraffin dehydrocyclization; naphthene dehydrogenation;
isomerization; hydrocracking; aromatic formation.

**Do not begin with a detailed molecular mechanism.** Use literature-supported
lumped or family-based reforming models.

**Do not write a `PlatformerRateEquation`.** The LHHW framework already exists
(`langmuir_hinshelwood_rate`, `adsorption_constant`, Arrhenius constants) —
this needs a reaction *network* over it.

The reactor train must support **interheating**: reforming is strongly
endothermic and the thermal effect is the defining feature of the unit.

**Outputs**: reformate flow/composition; aromatics yield; **H2 production**;
light gas; heat duty; catalyst/severity variables; elemental conservation.

The produced hydrogen **must enter the refinery-wide H2 network** and be usable
by hydrotreaters, hydrocracker, TGTU and other consumers. A reformer that
reports H2 as a number rather than a stream cannot do this.

Needs a reformate stabilizer — which needs the `ReboiledAbsorber` constructor
(P0 blocker).


## Programme constraints

No monolithic plant solvers. Reuse existing reaction/thermo/separation infrastructure. Conservation preserved across every representation change. Do not push to `main`.
title: Petchem: Catalytic reforming / Platformer

description: Found 2026-08-11 by correlation audit during op-4542. crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/array_control_vol_and_fluid_component_collections/one_d_fluid_array_with_lateral_coupling/fluid_component_calculation/mod.rs: enum doc (~L41-42) and constructor doc (~L91-92) say f_darcy = A + B*Re^C, but the implementation (~L152-158) returns a + b*Re^c directly as the fLDK value. Three confirmations fLDK is the true quantity: the sibling Pipe arm returns darcy*L/D + K; the Default impl uses (1,0,0) documented as 'the default is just K = 1'; darcy_friction_factor() for this variant is todo!(). A user following the doc would supply Darcy coefficients and get pressure drop wrong by roughly a factor of L/D. Fix is doc-side (rename/redocument as fLDK) plus decide what darcy_friction_factor() should do.
title: tuas: SimpleReynoldsPower documented as f_darcy but returns fLDK

description:
Maintainer request 2026-08-17: back up njoy-outram-park-fork's reference nuclear data to a dedicated GitHub repo, so the crate's fetch path has a fallback source when the direct IAEA download is blocked (GH issue #21: 'ENDF tsl data download blocked by network policy (IAEA 403)').

Decisions already made with the maintainer (via AskUserQuestion, 2026-08-17):
- Repo: theodoreOnzGit/njoy-nuclear-data, PUBLIC, no strong naming preference otherwise -- this name was my suggestion, maintainer said 'no preference', so treat it as provisional and confirm/rename if the maintainer wants something else when this is picked up.
- Scope: crates/../reference-data/endf/ (the 11 ENDF tapes currently at the outram-park-backend repo root, ~96 MB total, U-235 alone 35 MB -- see reference-data/endf/README.md for the existing provenance table to carry over) PLUS an empty placeholder folder + README stub for the future EXTENDED WMP library that docs/wmp-nuclide-manifest.md describes as planned ('ship in a separate sibling crate') but does not yet exist on disk anywhere in this checkout -- nothing to upload for that half yet, just reserve the layout.
- Implementation: a NEW code path in crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/src/acquire.rs -- add a git-sparse-checkout-based fallback tier to EndfCache (gated behind the existing net-fetch feature, or a new feature if that's cleaner) that clones/sparse-checks-out just the needed file from the backup repo when the direct IAEA HTTP fetch fails/403s. Recommend shelling out to the system 'git' binary (std::process::Command) rather than adding a Rust git-implementation crate (e.g. gix) as a new dependency -- this tier is already opt-in/dev-tooling via the feature gate, consistent with the module's existing 'a consumer that stays offline pulls none of these deps' design in acquire.rs's own module doc.

BLOCKER, hit 2026-08-17: mcp__github__create_repository failed -- 'POST https://api.github.com/user/repos: 403 Resource not accessible by integration'. The GitHub App connection this session uses does not have repo-creation scope. Two ways to unblock, maintainer's choice:
  (a) maintainer creates the empty repo (theodoreOnzGit/njoy-nuclear-data or their preferred name) manually on GitHub, then an agent session adds it via add_repo and pushes the data + writes the acquire.rs code, or
  (b) maintainer grants the GitHub connection repo-creation scope under claude.ai Settings -> Connectors.

Given the largest single file (U-235 tape, ~36 MB) and total payload (~96 MB), push the data via a local 'git clone' + 'git push' (git handles arbitrary file sizes over its own HTTP transport) rather than the push_files/create_or_update_file MCP tools, which take file content as a plain argument string and are not a good fit for tens of MB per file.

Not started: no repo exists yet, no acquire.rs code written yet. This bead is the parking spot for the whole task -- pick it up by first checking whether the repo now exists (ask the maintainer or check via list_repos) before doing anything else.
title: njoy: backup ENDF/WMP reference data to a new GitHub repo + git-sparse-checkout fallback fetch tier

    CONSTRUCTION (bead op-pej2) — an effectiveness/Q_max clamp, not a display fix
  - graceful salt-freeze handling: the physics thread pauses BEFORE the property

workspace for 'fhr_sim_v2' afterwards — the string appears in docs, beads and
commit-adjacent notes, not only in code.

description: Follow-ups surfaced by genfoam thermoMechanics mesh solve (op-p6p.11). (1) fvm::laplacian_vec only takes a scalar coefficient (2mu+lambda); an anisotropic stiffness needs a tensor-coefficient laplacian operator. (2) The field boundary layer offers only Dirichlet (FixedValue) and zero-gradient on D; a traction boundary condition (sigma.n = given, e.g. stress-free surface under thermal load where dD/dn != 0) is not expressible, so the stress-free free-thermal-expansion case can only be reached via a non-uniform temperature with Dirichlet ends. (3) fvc::grad_vec sets a zero-gradient output boundary, so the compact-normal-stress divSigmaExp correction carries no boundary-gradient info (exact on 1-D columns, approximate near 2-D/3-D boundaries). (4) No non-orthogonal gradient correction. See src/genfoam/thermo_mechanics/mesh_solve.rs limitations note.
title: basic-lib: add traction (sigma.n=0) BC on D and anisotropic (tensor-coeff) laplacian for thermo-mechanics
